references.text: Parallel text in Deuteronomy that also forbids eating pork because the pig has split hooves but does not chew the cud, and is therefore unclean.
Isaiah condemns those who eat pork as part of idolatrous worship and unclean practices.
The prophet mentions swine's blood as an example of abominable sacrifices.
Isaiah mentions those who eat pork among those who will be judged by the Lord.
Proverbs uses the pig as a symbol of uncleanness: a gold ring in a pig's snout is compared to a beautiful woman without discretion.
Jesus drives out demons that enter a herd of pigs, illustrating that pigs were still considered unclean animals in a Jewish context.
The prodigal son ends up feeding pigs, symbolizing his total degradation and distance from Jewish purity.
Peter's vision concerning unclean animals relates to the dietary laws in Leviticus and shows how the new covenant changes the understanding of clean and unclean.
